hooks.command: cat >/dev/null || true; command -v code-review-graph >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0; git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 && code-review-graph update --skip-flows --repo "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || true

cat >/dev/null || true; command -v code-review-graph >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0; git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 && code-review-graph status --repo "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || echo 'Not a git repo, skipping'

cat >/dev/null || true; printf '%s' '{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "SessionStart", "additionalContext": "Reply formatting (project rule, also in CLAUDE.md): in chat replies, do NOT use inline backtick code spans. They render as red monospace blocks in this terminal, and a paragraph naming several files and functions becomes an unreadable wall of them. Write file paths, function names, identifiers and line references as plain prose, e.g. dashboard/src/lib/job-filters.ts:231, isBlockingPickupStop, GUARD_MAX_AGE_MS. Fenced code blocks are fine. Prose only: this changes nothing about how code, commits or documentation are written."}, "suppressOutput": true}'
